newsitem.title: CANADA: Foothills Pipe sees meeting expansion target date.
newsitem.headline: Foothills Pipe sees meeting expansion target date.

text.p: The Canadian pipeline that carries natural gas to Northern Border Pipeline in the U.S. Midwest said on Thursday it expected no delays in meeting in-service dates for expansions of both systems.

Foothills Pipe Lines Ltd, which currently carries a third of the gas that flows to the U.S. from Canada, said an environmental approval granted last week by the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to Northern Border for its expansion and extension was a big milestone in the projects' development.
"Foothills and Northern Border anticipate no delays in the in-service date," Foothills vice-president Terry Cameron said in a statement.

The Northern Border project, which would add 700 million cubic feet a day of capacity to the pipeline and extend the system to Chicago from its current end point at Harper, Iowa, still requires a final FERC certificate.

Foothills, co-owned by NOVA Corp and Westcoast Energy Inc, carries 1.5 billion cubic feet of gas a day on its "Eastern Leg" to the Northern Border system at Monchy, Saskatchewan from McNeill, Alberta.
It has already won Canadian National Energy Board approval for its C$167 million corresponding expansion.

The projects, the first in what is shaping up to be a heated race to build billions of dollars worth of new pipeline capacity to the U.S. from Canada, have scheduled a November 1, 1998 in-service date.
Northern Border is 30-percent owned by TransCanada PipeLines Ltd and 70 percent owned by Enron Corp affiliate Northern Border Partners LP. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
